title: The acoustic Black Swan studio
summary: A little studio, thick brown wax, singing through a horn, and a kind engineer who played the takes back.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: But I was going to ask you about records. Do you remember what the studio looked like?
Yes. It was a little bitty studio.

Black Swan. And I wish I could remember that man that used to do the recording. He would do the recording. And they had big, thick wax, about like that. Big, thick brown wax. And it was a little window there, and this wax and recording thing was on that side, and I was in this little room singing through this little square window. Understand? Now, I'm in this little room.
In a horn, singing to a horn?

Through a horn, through a big horn. And it used to be a lot of shavings from the wax. That's how I recorded first. And this fellow took so much pains to try to see that it would be good. I wish I could remember his name; he was so nice, you know. He'd try to make my records good.
You didn't hear the records until they --
Yes, he'd play them again. Uh-huh, he'd make two or three of them, you know. Yes, he was -- I said that he was nice. Let me hear them. Wasn't that nice? He was a nice man.
I've been so lucky to always meet good people, nice people. You know. They say you get back in life what you give out, and I tried to give out something good all the time. Yes, that's right.
